primaryIssues: POST /api/checkout/create-order: N+1 DB calls inside a loop (per-item orderItem.update/create/delete) — will create many small writes and lock/connection pressure.
GET /api/products: unbounded findMany (no pagination) — full-table scans and large payloads.
Unindexed foreign keys on Order and other critical tables — lookups/joins will be slow under read/write load.
All issues from 10k scale amplified — N+1 on checkout and confirm-order, unbounded product list, and missing indexes will cause widespread DB saturation and timeouts.
Payment webhook performs order updates without an explicit transaction — risk of partial writes under concurrent webhooks.
No caching layer (Redis/memcached) combined with unbounded reads will cause catastrophic DB load.
Even with Prisma singleton, serverless concurrency will exhaust DB connections without an external pooler/proxy.
Long-running transactions with per-item updates (confirm-order) will increase lock contention and latency.

findings.title: N+1 DB writes in POST /api/checkout/create-order (per-item orderItem.update/create/delete inside loop)
findings.detail: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts executes prisma.orderItem.findMany and then performs prisma.orderItem.update, prisma.orderItem.create, and prisma.orderItem.delete inside a for-loop for each item. This issues multiple separate DB statements per order item on the request path.
findings.breaksAt: Estimated to fail under a few hundred concurrent checkout requests (~500 concurrent checkouts, lower with many items per order).
findings.fix: Replace per-item statements with bulk operations (createMany/updateMany) or single multi-row queries. If atomicity required, wrap batched operations in a transaction. Move non-essential per-item work off the critical path (background job).

traces.result: prisma.orderItem.findMany followed by prisma.orderItem.update/create/delete inside a for-loop (isInsideLoop true)

findings.title: N+1 updates inside transaction in POST /api/checkout/confirm-order (per-item tx.* updates)
findings.detail: src/app/api/checkout/confirm-order/route.ts uses prisma.$transaction but the transaction body performs per-item updates inside a for-loop (tx.order.update, tx.productColor.update, tx.product.update). Long transactions with many statements increase lock contention and latency.
findings.breaksAt: Will cause contention under moderate concurrency; expect problems starting around ~200 concurrent confirmations.
findings.fix: Minimize statements inside transactions: batch updates (updateMany or single UPDATE with CASE WHEN), avoid per-item tx calls, or move non-critical operations outside the transaction. Keep transactions short.

traces.result: prisma.$transaction present, with tx.order.update, tx.productColor.update, tx.product.update executed inside a for-loop (isInsideLoop true)

findings.title: Payment webhook updates order and cart without transaction — risk of partial writes
findings.detail: src/app/api/webhooks/razorpay/route.ts performs prisma.order.findFirst then prisma.order.update and prisma.cart.update without an explicit transaction wrapper. Failures during processing can leave order and cart out-of-sync.
findings.breaksAt: Concurrent or retried webhook deliveries (tens to hundreds) can produce inconsistent state; manifest under moderate webhook volume.
findings.fix: Wrap related writes in a transaction to ensure atomicity. Implement idempotency on webhook processing (store processed webhook IDs) and ensure lookups use indexed columns to avoid slow scans.

traces.result: prisma.order.findFirst, prisma.order.update, prisma.cart.update observed; no prisma.$transaction on the path

findings.title: Unbounded findMany on product list endpoint (GET /api/products) — missing pagination
findings.detail: src/app/api/products/route.ts calls prisma.product.findMany with no evidence of take/skip or cursor pagination. Returning entire product table on each request will cause full-table scans and large responses.
findings.breaksAt: Reading entire product table will break under high read concurrency (thousands of simultaneous requests); symptoms appear well before 100k users without caching and pagination.
findings.fix: Implement cursor-based or offset pagination, set sensible default and maximum limits, and cache list responses (CDN/Redis) for common queries.

traces.result: prisma.product.findMany with no pagination parameters detected

findings.title: Missing indexes on foreign keys and frequently queried columns in critical tables
findings.detail: prisma/schema.prisma contains only 4 explicit indexes across 18 tables. Several foreign key columns used by critical flows are not indexed (e.g., Order.userId, Order.couponId, Order.razorpayOrderId/razorpayPaymentId). Lack of indexes on FK and lookup columns will cause slow joins/filters under load.
findings.breaksAt: Will cause full-table scans and slow queries under moderate-to-high traffic (tens of thousands of users and many concurrent order/lookups).
findings.fix: Add indexes on columns used in WHERE/JOIN conditions (e.g., Order.userId, Order.razorpayOrderId, Order.razorpayPaymentId, Order.couponId). Use composite indexes where queries filter on multiple columns. Re-check with EXPLAIN for heavy queries.

traces.result: schema extraction shows totalIndexes:4 across 18 tables; many FK columns have isIndexed:false

findings.title: No application cache detected for read-heavy endpoints
findings.detail: Dependencies and code show no Redis or memcached integration. Product list and product detail endpoints are read-heavy; without a caching layer every read hits the DB increasing load and costs.
findings.breaksAt: At large scale (100k+ users) read traffic will saturate the DB; caching would mitigate load and increase throughput.
findings.fix: Introduce Redis (or managed caching) for product lists, category caches, and hot item lookups. Use CDN caching for public product lists and short TTLs with proper cache invalidation on updates.

traces.result: products listing functions are high-frequency imports (CategoryPage, product listing)

findings.title: Prisma client uses serverless singleton but no external pooler detected
findings.detail: src/lib/prisma.ts uses globalThis singleton for PrismaClient (good serverless pattern). checkConnectionPool shows no external pooler (Prisma Data Proxy, PgBouncer, Neon) and no explicit pool settings in DATABASE_URL. Without an external pooler, serverless concurrency can still exhaust DB connections on large bursts.
findings.breaksAt: High serverless concurrency (hundreds to thousands of concurrent function instances) can exhaust DB connections depending on DB limits and connection churn.
findings.fix: Consider Prisma Data Proxy or an external pooler (pgbouncer) or use a managed DB with proper connection handling for serverless workloads. Monitor connection counts and tune DB settings.

traces.result: exports prisma singleton using globalThis; no pool settings

summary.topConcern: POST /api/checkout/create-order has per-item DB writes inside a loop (orderItem.update/create/delete) — N+1 on every checkout will break under moderate concurrency.
summary.estimatedScaleCeiling: ~500 concurrent checkouts before DB write saturation; without caching or indexing the overall app is unlikely to scale past tens of thousands of active users.
